prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

LOS ANGELES, California (CNN)  -- Media maven Oprah Winfrey earned 10 times more than Angelina Jolie last year, but the actress bumped the talk show host from the top spot on Forbes' 2009 Celebrity 100 list just released by the business magazine. Angelina Jolie has ousted Oprah Winfrey from the No. 1 spot on Forbes' 2009 Celebrity 100 list. Jolie's fame, evidenced by magazine covers and TV, radio, newspaper and Web stories, outweighed Winfrey's, giving her the edge as "the most powerful celebrity in the world" based on Forbes' formula, Forbes Senior Editor Matthew Miller said. Winfrey, who was at the top for two years straight, grossed $275 million last year, compared with Jolie's $27 million, Miller said. "We try and measure a celebrity's power, and we look at two metrics to do that," Miller said. "We look at money, and we look at fame." A world tour, which helped Madonna pull in $110 million, and a bumper crop of tabloid gossip pushed the Material Girl into the third spot, up from her 21st ranking on last year's list. Beyonce Knowles held steady in fourth, same as last year, with $87 million in income from her multiplatform empire, Miller said. Forbes leveraged the singer-actresses fame by placing her on this week's cover. A bad knee kept Tiger Woods off the PGA tour over the past year and lowered him to the fifth spot on the Forbes list. The golfer, still the highest-paid athlete in the world, was second last year. Bruce Springsteen's tour landed the Boss in sixth, while director Steven Spielberg's latest Indiana Jones movie helped him to seventh place. Actress Jennifer Aniston and her ex-husband, Brad Pitt, were eighth and ninth, respectively, on the strength of successful movies and tabloid headlines. Basketballer Kobe Bryant's endorsements and popularity, boosted by his play on the U.S. Olympic team, jumped to the 10th spot. Miller said Forbes' has spent a great amount of time compiling the list for the past decade because "celebrities play an ever increasing role in everyone's lives, whether we like it or not." "Celebrities are brands, and they are marketing to us and there's stuff we consume off of them, from movies to albums to concerts to books to speaking tours to everything in between, and we sort of all buy into it," he said. The income figures used are gross numbers and do not take into account what goes to agents, managers, taxes and expenses, Miller said. "It can be very expensive to be a celebrity," he said. "What they're taking home to their personal checking accounts is far less than their gross earnings." The list, which has been "put through our special sauce of earnings and fame," is used as a barometer of who has the real power in Hollywood, Miller said. "When you look at the components of fame and earnings, you can get a good vibe as to who's important this year and who's not," he said. "Angelina Jolie is, by far, the most famous celebrity on the planet," he said. "There's not a day that goes by where she's not on the cover of a tabloid magazine or a regular magazine. There's not day that goes by when people are not talking about her philanthropy or her relationship with Brad Pitt or her movies or her children. All of that lends to a more popular, more robust and, frankly, more valuable brand." Miller estimated that Jolie was on about 20 to 30 times more magazine covers last year than Winfrey. It's normal for celebs to fall down or off the list for a year if they are between projects, he said. One newcomer to the list of top 100 celebrities is Barack Obama, debuting at 49. Obama is the first sitting head of state to appear in Forbes' Celebrity 100 rankings. CNN's Jim Roope contributed to this report.

outputs.L1:
**LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) —** Media maven Oprah Winfrey earned 10 times more than Angelina Jolie last year, but the actress displaced the talk-show host from the top spot on Forbes’ newly released 2009 Celebrity 100 list.

Jolie’s fame—as reflected in magazine covers and television, radio, newspaper and Web stories—outweighed Winfrey’s, giving her the edge as “the most powerful celebrity in the world” under Forbes’ formula, according to Forbes Senior Editor Matthew Miller.

Winfrey, who had topped the list for two consecutive years, grossed $275 million last year, compared with Jolie’s $27 million, Miller said.

“We try and measure a celebrity’s power, and we look at two metrics to do that,” Miller said. “We look at money, and we look at fame.”

A world tour that helped Madonna earn $110 million, along with a bumper crop of tabloid gossip, propelled the Material Girl into third place, up from No. 21 on last year’s list.

Beyoncé Knowles held steady at No. 4, the same position she occupied last year, with $87 million in income from her multiplatform empire, Miller said. Forbes capitalized on the singer-actress’s fame by featuring her on this week’s cover.

A knee injury kept Tiger Woods off the PGA Tour over the past year and dropped him to fifth place on the Forbes list. The golfer, who remains the world’s highest-paid athlete, ranked second last year.

Bruce Springsteen’s tour landed the Boss in sixth place, while director Steven Spielberg’s latest Indiana Jones movie helped propel him to seventh.

Actress Jennifer Aniston and her ex-husband, Brad Pitt, ranked eighth and ninth, respectively, on the strength of successful movies and tabloid headlines.

Basketball player Kobe Bryant rose to the 10th spot, boosted by endorsements, popularity and his performance on the U.S. Olympic team.

Miller said Forbes has devoted considerable time to compiling the list over the past decade because “celebrities play an ever-increasing role in everyone’s lives, whether we like it or not.”

“Celebrities are brands, and they are marketing to us, and there’s stuff we consume off of them, from movies to albums to concerts to books to speaking tours to everything in between, and we sort of all buy into it,” he said.

The income figures represent gross earnings and do not account for payments to agents and managers, taxes or expenses, Miller said.

“It can be very expensive to be a celebrity,” he said. “What they’re taking home to their personal checking accounts is far less than their gross earnings.”

The list, which has been “put through our special sauce of earnings and fame,” serves as a barometer of who holds real power in Hollywood, Miller said.

“When you look at the components of fame and earnings, you can get a good vibe as to who’s important this year and who’s not,” he said.

“Angelina Jolie is, by far, the most famous celebrity on the planet,” he said. “There’s not a day that goes by when she’s not on the cover of a tabloid magazine or a regular magazine. There’s not a day that goes by when people are not talking about her philanthropy or her relationship with Brad Pitt or her movies or her children. All of that lends to a more popular, more robust and, frankly, more valuable brand.”

Miller estimated that Jolie appeared on roughly 20 to 30 times more magazine covers than Winfrey did last year.

It is normal for celebrities to fall lower on—or drop off—the list for a year when they are between projects, he said.

One newcomer to the list of the top 100 celebrities is Barack Obama, who debuted at No. 49. Obama is the first sitting head of state to appear in Forbes’ Celebrity 100 rankings.

CNN’s Jim Roope contributed to this report.

LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) — Although Oprah Winfrey made 10 times as much money as Angelina Jolie last year, Jolie displaced the talk-show host at the top of Forbes magazine’s newly released 2009 Celebrity 100 rankings.

Forbes Senior Editor Matthew Miller said Jolie’s extensive public visibility—including appearances on magazine covers and coverage across television, radio, newspapers and the internet—gave her the advantage under the publication’s formula, making her the world’s most powerful celebrity.

Winfrey had held first place for two consecutive years. She grossed $275 million last year, while Jolie earned $27 million, according to Miller.

Forbes evaluates celebrity power using two main measures: income and fame, Miller explained.

Madonna rose from No. 21 the previous year to third place, aided by a world tour that generated $110 million and a surge of tabloid attention. Beyoncé Knowles remained in fourth place, the same position she occupied last year, after earning $87 million through her various business and entertainment ventures. Forbes also capitalized on the singer-actress’s popularity by featuring her on that week’s cover.

Tiger Woods dropped from second to fifth after a knee injury kept him away from the PGA Tour during the previous year. Despite the decline, he remained the world’s highest-paid athlete.

Bruce Springsteen’s touring success put “the Boss” in sixth place. Director Steven Spielberg ranked seventh, helped by the latest Indiana Jones film. Jennifer Aniston and her former husband Brad Pitt took eighth and ninth place, respectively, because of successful movies and frequent tabloid coverage.

Kobe Bryant moved into the No. 10 position, driven by endorsements and increased popularity resulting from his performance with the U.S. Olympic basketball team.

Miller said Forbes has devoted substantial effort to producing the annual list over the past decade because celebrities have become increasingly influential in people’s lives, whether the public welcomes that influence or not.

He described celebrities as brands that market themselves to consumers through films, albums, concerts, books, speaking engagements and many other products and activities. In his view, the public participates in and supports that marketplace.

The earnings listed by Forbes are gross amounts and do not subtract payments to agents and managers or the costs of taxes and other expenses, Miller noted. Celebrity life can be costly, he said, so the sums stars actually deposit into their personal accounts are much lower than their reported gross income.

According to Miller, Forbes combines earnings and fame using its own proprietary formula, and the resulting list serves as an indicator of who truly holds power in Hollywood. Looking at both factors, he said, provides a useful sense of which celebrities matter in a given year and which do not.

Miller called Jolie “by far” the most famous celebrity in the world. He said she appeared almost constantly on tabloid and mainstream magazine covers and was discussed daily because of her charitable work, relationship with Brad Pitt, movies and children. Together, those elements made her public brand more prominent, stronger and ultimately more valuable.

He estimated that Jolie appeared on roughly 20 to 30 times as many magazine covers as Winfrey during the previous year.

Miller added that it is common for celebrities to drop in the rankings—or disappear from the list for a year—when they are between projects.

Barack Obama was among the newcomers to the top 100, entering at No. 49. He became the first sitting head of state included in Forbes’ Celebrity 100 rankings.

CNN’s Jim Roope contributed to the report.

## Forbes releases its 2009 Celebrity 100

Forbes unveiled its 2009 **Celebrity 100** ranking on **June 3, 2009**, naming **Angelina Jolie** the world’s most powerful celebrity. Jolie displaced Oprah Winfrey, who had led the previous two editions.

### How the ranking worked

The Celebrity 100 was a **power ranking, not simply a list of the highest-paid stars**. Forbes combined:

- **Estimated pretax earnings** during the preceding 12 months—roughly June 2008 through June 2009—from films, television, music, sports, publishing, endorsements and other entertainment-related work.
- A **“fame” score** measuring exposure in print, television, radio and online media, including web and social-network visibility.

Earnings estimates were assembled with help from industry sources such as agents, managers, lawyers and producers. The combined money-and-media formula explains why Jolie, with estimated earnings of **$27 million**, ranked ahead of Winfrey, who earned an estimated **$275 million** but had a lower overall fame score.

### 2009 top 10

| Rank | Celebrity | Estimated earnings |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | Angelina Jolie | $27 million |
| 2 | Oprah Winfrey | $275 million |
| 3 | Madonna | $110 million |
| 4 | Beyoncé Knowles | $87 million |
| 5 | Tiger Woods | $110 million |
| 6 | Bruce Springsteen | $70 million |
| 7 | Steven Spielberg | $150 million |
| 8 | Jennifer Aniston | $25 million |
| 9 | Brad Pitt | $28 million |
| 10 | Kobe Bryant | $45 million |

Jolie’s first-place finish reflected intense global attention surrounding her films, humanitarian work and family life. Madonna and Springsteen benefited from major tours, while Woods, Bryant and Beyoncé combined strong earnings with extensive media exposure.

### Barack Obama’s debut

President **Barack Obama entered the Celebrity 100 for the first time at No. 49**. His inclusion followed the extraordinary publicity surrounding the 2008 presidential campaign, his historic election and his first months in office.

Forbes credited Obama with about **$2.5 million in earnings**, largely from royalties on his bestselling books rather than his presidential salary. His income was modest by Celebrity 100 standards, but his overwhelming press, broadcast and online presence lifted him into the ranking. His appearance also demonstrated the list’s broad definition of celebrity power: public visibility and cultural influence could compensate for comparatively low earnings.
